security_audit.summary: Four static findings are confirmed because the skill directs agents to mutate an external task backend. The command on line 52 embeds a user-provided description in shell command text, creating a command injection risk unless arguments are passed safely. The other 16 findings are Markdown formatting, placeholders, read-only listing, or ordinary questions, and no additional semantic threat was found.

remediation.issue: The incident description is placed inside a shell command and may contain command substitution or quoting characters.
remediation.suggestion: Pass the description as one literal process argument without shell interpolation, and validate generated task identifiers before use.

remediation.issue: Parent creation and task completion mutate the configured task backend.
remediation.suggestion: Show the planned mutation and request confirmation before creating hierarchy records or changing an incident to completed.

content.user_title: Turn Workflow Mistakes Into Lasting Lessons
content.value_statement: Repeated workflow mistakes waste time and weaken consistency. This skill records each incident, confirms its root cause and fix, and stores the lesson for reuse.
actual_capabilities: Lists open mistake incidents from the configured task backend.
Creates a shared milestone and epic hierarchy when required.
Records a confirmed mistake as an in-progress bug task.
Collects user confirmation for the root cause and corrective action.
Appends a dated lesson to the selected learned-memory topic.
Marks the incident completed after applying the confirmed fix.
limitations: Requires a configured task backend and the beans command.
Supports project memory under the .groove directory only.
Depends on user confirmation to identify an accurate root cause and fix.
Redirects fixes for managed skills files into learned memory instead of editing those files.

use_cases.title: Prevent Repeated Agent Errors
use_cases.description: Record a coding assistant mistake, confirm its cause, and preserve a rule that guides later work.
use_cases.target_user: Software developers using AI coding agents

use_cases.title: Maintain Team Workflow Memory
use_cases.description: Convert a recurring process failure into a dated lesson stored with the project.

use_cases.title: Review Open Improvement Incidents
use_cases.description: List unresolved mistakes from the task backend before planning corrective work.

prompt_templates.title: List Open Mistakes
prompt_templates.prompt: List the open workflow mistake incidents for this project.

prompt_templates.title: Record a Mistake
prompt_templates.prompt: Record this mistake: I changed a generated file instead of its source file. Ask me to confirm the root cause and fix.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve a Repeated Error
prompt_templates.prompt: Log the repeated test setup error, propose its root cause from our context, and wait for confirmation before applying the fix.
prompt_templates.scenario: Root cause analysis with a corrective action

prompt_templates.title: Graduate a Complex Lesson
prompt_templates.prompt: Document the deployment workflow failure, confirm the permanent fix, store a dated lesson under the best topic, and close the incident.

output_examples.input: Record that I fixed a generated skill file directly.
output_examples.output: Incident resolved. The confirmed lesson was added to the anti-patterns memory topic, and the task was marked completed.

best_practices: Describe the observed mistake with concrete actions and outcomes.
Confirm the root cause and corrective action before changing files.
Choose a learned topic that future agents can find easily.
anti_patterns: Do not create an incident without explicit user confirmation.
Do not close an incident before identifying its root cause.
Do not edit managed skills files when learned memory is the supported destination.

faq.question: What does this skill record?
faq.answer: It records workflow mistakes as task-backend incidents with a confirmed root cause, fix, and reusable lesson.

faq.question: Can it list unresolved mistakes?
faq.answer: Yes. The list mode displays in-progress bug tasks beneath the shared Mistakes parent.

faq.question: Does it require a task backend?
faq.answer: Yes. The project must configure a supported backend before incidents can be listed or created.

faq.question: Where are learned lessons stored?
faq.answer: Lessons are appended under dated headings in topic files within .groove/memory/learned.

faq.question: Will it change files automatically?
faq.answer: It proposes a fix and asks for confirmation before applying the relevant project edit.

faq.question: Can it modify managed skill files?
faq.answer: No. It redirects those lessons to the anti-patterns memory file because the skills directory is managed.
